subject: Inference edge fencing: network walkthrough & evidence bundle
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-09-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: edge/ingress fencing for Private deployment

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this — Acme's security review team had a couple of focused asks after the SOC 2 questionnaire: they want a short walkthrough that explains how Redwood protects the inference 'edge' (ingress endpoints) and how tenant isolation is enforced for Private/Dedicated deployments, specifically:

- A simple network diagram showing external ingress, LB/edge, firewall/NGW layers, and any egress inspection points.
- Evidence of ACLs or NSG exports that demonstrate tenant demarcation (we don't need full configs, just sample rules and explanation).
- An operational playbook for a fail-open vs fail-closed scenario at the edge (how would you respond to a compromised edge node?).

Could you share a short walkthrough and any diagrams or playbooks you can provide? We aim to close this section of the SIG by EOD Thu.

Cheers,
John
Security Engineer
Acme Corp
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-07T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: edge/ingress fencing for Private deployment

John —

Appreciate the clear asks. I'm looping in Karthik (network/architecture) and Soojin (private deployments) and will assemble:

1) A concise network diagram highlighting ingress -> edge load balancer -> perimeter NGW -> tenant routing (I've sketched a v2 diagram and will attach).
2) A sanitized ACL export (three sample rules showing deny/allow semantics by tenant VLAN/tag).
3) A short operational playbook (fail-open vs fail-closed) plus escalation runbook.

We'll attach the artifacts and a short narration. If you want us to walk through this live, we can schedule a 30-min session.

Target to you: same day (attachments + narrative).

—Grace
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-07T14:18:00Z
Subject: Fwd: artifacts for Acme — edge fencing bundle (draft)

Folks — attaching the first-pass artifacts. I've sanitized tenant IDs and removed internal IP ranges that are not relevant. Key notes inline: 

- edge-fence-network-diagram-v2.png: shows provider ingress (TLS termination at LB), DDoS scrubbing tier (optional), regional NGW cluster, and per-tenant overlay networks terminating at dedicated inference pools for Private deployments. The diagram also annotates where KV-cache prefixes are stored and how flow logs are collected.

- private-deploy-isolation-playbook.pdf: two-page playbook describing detection, isolation (quarantine of an affected node), routing policy rollback, and fallback routing to a cold standby model variant. It also lists the granular steps we take to avoid cross-tenant KV cache leakage (cache invalidation tokens + per-tenant namespaces).

- acl-export-20260906.csv: sanitized sample lines showing source/destination/port/action with a tenant_tag column. We use an infra tagging system that maps tenant_tag -> tenant overlay. Enforcement is at the NGW + host-level iptables/nftables with template-based rules.

Questions for the external review we might anticipate:
1) How do we ensure egress controls for private deployments that have customer-managed VPC peering? (Answer: egress inspection via regional proxy, and enforced egress ACLs at the NGW; details in the playbook.)
2) What about patching and rebuilds of edge nodes? (Answer: immutable images, automated rebuilds coordinated through our Dedicated rolling policy; steps in playbook.)

I recommend a short annotated playback with Acme security. Grace, want me to join the call?

-Karthik
Senior Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edge-fence-network-diagram-v2.png, private-deploy-isolation-playbook.pdf, acl-export-20260906.csv
From: John Doe <john.doe@acmecorp.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: 2026-09-08T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: edge/ingress fencing for Private deployment

Grace/Karthik —

Thanks, this looks good at a glance. A couple quick clarifying requests from our reviewers:

- Can you add a one-paragraph explanation in the diagram that calls out the failure modes (edge node compromise, LB config drift, mis-tagged tenant traffic) and the immediate containment action for each?
- On the ACL sample: can you show an example deny-by-default baseline + the explicit tenant-allow lines (so our auditors can see the policy orientation)?

If you can drop small updates (diagram + one extra CSV row) we'll be able to mark this as 'evidence provided' in the SIG matrix. A short 20-min sync would be fine too.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—John
Acme Corp Security
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

Thanks for the feedback. Karthik pushed a minor revision to the diagram and added a short failure-modes legend; Vanessa added a deny-by-default example row to the ACL CSV.
